claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi can be prepared in a homogeneous simple solid-solution state.
The proposed initial state has minimal pre-existing dislocation structures.
Rapid dynamic recovery during room-temperature deformation governs the low hardness and strength of equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Dynamic recovery causes low dislocation accumulation and limited work hardening at room temperature.
Cryogenic temperature suppresses dynamic recovery in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Suppression of recovery at cryogenic temperature permits greater dislocation entanglement and enhanced strengthening.
The proposed controlled comparison tests as-cast and thermomechanically pre-worked samples at 300 K and 77 K using tensile testing and nanoindentation.
The deformation tests are specified at an approximately constant strain rate of 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Dislocation formation, reorganization, and annihilation are the structural mediators of the proposed dynamic-recovery behavior.
At room temperature, the homogeneous solid solution facilitates easy dislocation glide.
Room-temperature deformation produces rapid dislocation annihilation and cell formation.
Rapid recovery prevents formation of the dislocation forests needed for substantial strain hardening.
At 300 K, the samples will exhibit low dislocation density, minimal strain hardening, low hardness, and low strength.
Relative to 300 K, testing at 77 K will produce greater dislocation accumulation or entanglement.
Relative to 300 K, testing at 77 K will produce higher hardness and yield strength.
The hypothesis is bounded to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state, temperatures from 77 K to 300 K, and strain rates near 1×10^-3 s^-1.
Minor deformation twinning may occur concurrently and complicate interpretation of dislocation-density and property measurements.
Comparable dislocation density, strain hardening, and hardness at 300 K and 77 K would falsify the proposed room-temperature dynamic-recovery explanation.
